repository.name: fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template
repository.workload: Not supplied — a project scaffold/template, not a deployed service with known traffic.

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from docs/evaluation.md §3.2 (Round 1) and §3.10 (independent blind pass, same repository, same finding reproduced). Weaker evidence than an independently-established annotation — see benchmark/README.md.

expected.mechanism: GET /items declares `limit: int = 100` as a plain default with no Query(le=...) enforced upper bound. A default is not an enforced maximum: a caller can request an arbitrarily large page, and the query cost grows with the requested limit rather than a fixed cap. Independently confirms the identical pattern documented in docs/examples/fastapi-postgres.md and application/api.md §1, found here in a real, actively maintained template with no connection to this project.

forbidden.why_not: The `node` signal fires because this monorepo has a frontend/ directory with its own package.json and node_modules — those tokens cannot distinguish a Node.js backend runtime from front-end tooling sitting in the same repository. For a backend performance review this would be a false attribution of the backend runtime; the actual backend is Python/FastAPI. See docs/evaluation.md §3.2 and §3.3.

The `rest` signal's Go-framework tokens (gin, echo) matched only incidentally: `gin` inside the English word "logging" in compose.override.yml, and `echo` inside ordinary shell `echo` commands in CI workflow YAML. Neither Go web framework is present anywhere in this Python/TypeScript repository. See docs/evaluation.md §3.2 and §3.3, and tests/test_detect_stack_regressions.py's LockfileHashCollisionTests for the fixed regression.
